question: Two complaints arrive that nobody connects at first. In the first, a piece of the interface that had already been dismissed does a little more work after it had said it wanted nothing further - once writing into state belonging to a screen that was no longer on display. In the second, rarer one, a piece that had never said anything of the kind is simply passed over when a change goes out, and keeps showing what it held before, until something unrelated later forces it to catch up. Both happen only when one participant stops caring at the same moment others are being told that something changed, and which of the two complaints you get depends on where that participant happened to sit relative to the others. Two of these libraries already treat this as ordinary rather than exceptional, and decide who is owed the news before any of it goes out, so that a departure during delivery changes nothing for anyone else. Which files let a departure mid-delivery disturb who else gets told, and which own the rule they must be brought in line with?
anchor: Defect side iterates a live listener collection during dispatch (zustand vanilla.ts, query subscribable.ts + subclasses, tldraw Store.ts). Contract side settles recipients first: redux ensureCanMutateNextListeners copy-on-write, jotai accumulates into a fresh callbacks Set. v1 of this question scored Opus-bare 1.000 because it described the mechanism ('walk a collection edited underneath them'); v2 states only the two user-visible symptoms. Gold now includes four files with no iteration vocabulary at all (redux types/store.ts, query types.ts, jotai vanilla/store.ts, zustand react.ts) which no mechanism-grep can reach.
